---
id: "smk-13"
title: "Barn owl"
---

The barn owl is a medium-sized owl with a heart-shaped white face, pale underparts and golden-brown upper parts, found on every continent except Antarctica. It hunts at night over open country such as farmland, grassland and marsh, flying low and silently thanks to the soft edges of its feathers, and it locates small mammals such as voles and mice by sound alone; its asymmetrically placed ears allow it to pinpoint prey in complete darkness. Barn owls nest in tree hollows, cliff cavities and, as the name suggests, in barns and other buildings, and they readily use nest boxes. A pair may raise several chicks in a year when rodents are plentiful. The species does not hoot but produces a long, harsh screech. Barn owl numbers in Europe and North America have been affected by intensive agriculture, road traffic and rodent poisons.
